name: Zimmah
overview: Zimmah was a male Levite identified as the son of Jahath, belonging to the Gershonite branch of the tribe of Levi. As a Gershonite, he was part of the descendants of Gershon, son of Levi, who were assigned specific duties related to the tabernacle service. His lineage places him within the priestly tribe set apart for service to God.
namesAndTitles: The name Zimmah means 'consider' or 'plan,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew proper name. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but its meaning may imply thoughtful or deliberate qualities.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zimmah as the son of Jahath. It is also inferred that Joah was his father, suggesting a generational lineage within the Levite family. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zimmah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, specifically as a Gershonite descendant responsible for aspects of tabernacle service. His mention helps preserve the record of priestly families dedicated to God's worship, underscoring the continuity of divine service through generations. This genealogical detail contributes to understanding the organization and heritage of the Levites in Israel.
